claim: Cramming demonstrates that a single consumer GPU with no interconnect at all can train a transformer language model from scratch to BERT-base-class GLUE performance in 24 hours, establishing the zero-interconnect limiting case of the CMP 170HX feasibility envelope.
stance_target: The repo's premise that meaningful training experiments are feasible on a box with no NVLink and no P2P, because the degenerate single-GPU case is already productive
scope_conditions: Masked-language-model pretraining from scratch, 24-hour wall-clock budget, single GPU (RTX 2080 Ti / A4000 / A6000), GLUE evaluation
quoted_support: We investigate the downstream performance achievable with a transformer-based language model trained completely from scratch with masked language modeling for a single day on a single consumer GPU... we provide evidence that even in this constrained setting, performance closely follows scaling laws observed in large-compute settings.

claim: Per-token training efficiency depends strongly on model size but not on transformer architecture type, so architecture modifications only improve outcomes insofar as they raise throughput at constant parameter count.
stance_target: The repo's claim that architecture axes (MoE, Engram, CSA2) must be evaluated on throughput-per-FLOP, not on intrinsic per-token quality
scope_conditions: Low-compute regime, single-GPU 24-hour budget, multiple transformer architecture variants at matched parameter counts
quoted_support: Per-token efficiency of training depends strongly on model size, but not transformer type. Furthermore, smaller models learn less efficiently, and this largely mitigates any throughput gains... we can boost performance by finding architecture modifications that speed up gradient computation while keeping the parameter count nearly constant.

claim: Cramming found no benefit from CPU or NVMe offloading in the single-GPU low-compute setting, undermining offloading as a workaround for a per-card memory ceiling.
stance_target: The idea that host-side offloading can rescue a model that does not fit in 64 GB of HBM per card
scope_conditions: Single-GPU training with automated mixed precision, offloading implementations from Ren et al. 2021 and Rasley et al. 2020
quoted_support: We find no benefit from offloading (Ren et al., 2021; Rasley et al., 2020) in our setting.

claim: The ablation accounting in Cramming attributes roughly 2 GLUE points to architecture changes, 1 point to data changes, and 0.5 point to training-recipe changes — architecture dominates, but only because it buys throughput at fixed parameter count.
stance_target: How much of a small-scale run's outcome is attributable to each of the repo's four experiment axes
scope_conditions: Cramming ablation study, BERT-base architecture, 24-hour budget
quoted_support: we ultimately find about two percentage points gained in average GLUE score through architectural changes, one percentage point in data changes, and half a precentage point in training modifications.

claim: Cramming uses sequence length 128 with packed sequences, yielding micro-batches of 64-96 on an 11 GB RTX 2080 Ti that are accumulated into larger batches, and single-epoch training is feasible at this budget.
stance_target: The repo's premise that small per-card memory can be compensated by gradient accumulation at short sequence lengths
scope_conditions: Cramming implementation, BERT-base variants, packed 128-token sequences
quoted_support: We pack tokenized data into randomized sequences of length 128 and separate unrelated fragments by <sep>... For the targeted compute settings, this sequence length results in micro-batch sizes of 64 to 96 for most variations of the base BERT architecture on the gtx2080ti, which we will accumulate into larger batch sizes.

claim: FlashAttention is only re-enabled for the final architecture variant in Cramming, after all ablations are run on plain PyTorch operators, which means the reported ablation results are not FlashAttention-dependent.
stance_target: Whether FlashAttention-class kernels are a prerequisite for the small-scale results the repo wants to reproduce
quoted_support: Only after choosing a final architecture variant, we then re-enable the efficient attention kernel described in Dao et al. (2022).

claim: Cramming's compute budget is roughly 15x smaller than the 8x V100 server-node BERT-in-24-hours baseline it compares against, which quantifies how far a single-GPU budget sits below a small multi-GPU node.
stance_target: How a 5-card CMP 170HX box compares in effective compute to a conventional small training node
scope_conditions: Comparison against Izsak et al. 2021, 8x V100 node
quoted_support: Izsak et al. (2021) choose a BERTLARGE architecture... We re-evaluate this setup as a baseline setting for our own compute budget (which is about 15x smaller).

claim: Cramming's peak-throughput table records single-GPU BERT-reproduction budgets of 8 FLOP-days on an RTX A4000 and 13 on an RTX A6000, giving concrete per-card compute anchors for a 24-hour run.
stance_target: Whether a 64 GB card at ~162 TFLOPS bf16 (CMP 170HX) can complete a BERT-class run in a day
scope_conditions: Cramming Table 1, single-GPU BERT variations, 1 day
quoted_support: BERT variation, 1 rtxa4000, 1 day, 8; Our Setup 3, BERT variation, 1 rtxa6000, 1 day, 13.
